$comment: Desk grade (store pages, Steam review API quotes, press, aggregators). NOT hands-on play; no claim of having played or listened.

package.basis: Desk only: Steam store page/appdetails and DLC listings, Steam review API (165 English reviews sampled, all-language 767/830 positive), Steam news, vaporlens aggregate and a TrendingNow review via search snippet; not played.

fun.source: desk estimate: a compact action ARPG that turns idle only mid-late (5-10 h); strong build-making but a reported wall after level 50 and a cluttered UI; below Melvor (65.4), well above a mediocre idle RPG (30.8). Median positive reviewer ~25 h.

evidence.quote: The pixel art is pretty good while being minimalist
The game's pixel art style is noted as simple, novel, and charming
While the graphics may not be groundbreaking

dims.note: Coherent minimalist pixel art on a grey platform; readable, not a screenshot-seller.

evidence.quote: The clear, crisp animations make combat easy to follow, even during hectic moments
a black void surrounding a grey platform and alot of bright flashing for skills

dims.note: Real-time action animation; some eye-strain reports.

evidence.quote: The user interface is described as horrible, cluttered, and not user-friendly
There are a lot of missing tooltips like that.
the translation is sometimes really bad and leaves you completely unable to figure out what something does

dims.note: Loot filter and build presets praised, but stats hidden and translation poor.

evidence.quote: the lobby music is super chill and i love it
I do wish there was more/different music.
All background music of Dark Hunting Ground, a total of 8 songs.

dims.note: From review consensus only; never listened.

evidence.quote: The tutorial is pretty well done, it may seem daunting at first
Game is really front heavy with the mechanics and a lot of reading
an rpg that you can automate later on (like 5-10h deep

dims.note: Core act instant and auto-pickup from the start, but idle automation arrives hours in.

evidence.quote: It starts off really strong ... then it slogs down to an absolute standstill crawl
Eventually that all comes crashing to a halt when you hit level 50.
Things unlock basically every step of the way until endgame

dims.note: Consistent 'strong start, grind wall at level 50 / third tier' across reviews and aggregator.

evidence.quote: Every skill can be socketed with 7 Slates, drastically reshaping its form and effect.
Build-making is extremely satisfying.
Players are restricted by the ability to only set three skills

dims.note: Six archetypes, slates, relics, Abyssal Eyes, custom hunting grounds; '3 skills' cap and stat-stacking late.

evidence.quote: $12.99; DLC: Druid Class Pack $4.99, Skin Supporter Pack $4.99, Soundtrack $1.99
You can also afk farm mats for crafting if you want to
my PC save from the Demo ... does not sync in the cloud like it says

dims.note: No paid skips; AFK farming only while running (no offline sim found); a paid class DLC.

evidence.quote: alot of bright flashing for skills
skip reward screens, and adjust skill effect transparency

dims.note: Loot rain and skill flash; inferred from store and reviews.

evidence.quote: The game suffers from significant lag, especially in the late game
cant have a single session without atleast 1 blue screen crash
BUG FIX 1.6.4: Fixed a bug that could cause save files to malfunction

dims.note: Lag, crashes and a save bug patched; kill not set (reports not a reproduced pattern).

evidence.quote: Theres only 5 bosses, but they also get more attacks the more you progress
if you played the Demo you've seen all of the game
1.6.5 UPDATES: Torment Difficulty and Druid DLC

dims.note: Endless Abyss and difficulty tiers; small boss roster, repeating arenas.

evidence.quote: A minimalist pixel-action RPG built around loot and power.
Incremental/idle POE? with Torchlight infinite corruption mechanics?
Windows and macOS; 9 languages incl. Simplified Chinese, English, French, Japanese, Korean
Customize keybinds, skip reward screens, and adjust skill effect transparency
The game currently lacks proper controller support

dims.note: Two platforms, many (poorly translated) languages, some options.

learn.practice: Make automation a build component (an auto-cast Slate socketed into a skill), so going idle is itself a build decision.
learn.evidence: https://store.steampowered.com/app/2494810/ — 'Go from hands-on farming to fully automated looting as you refine your systems'

learn.practice: Unlock a new system at each difficulty tier (talents, Dark Tree, Chaos Atlas) and name it, then avoid DHG's lapse of letting unlocks stop at the wall.
learn.evidence: https://steamcommunity.com/app/2494810/reviews (recommendation 234243250; via store.steampowered.com/appreviews/2494810?json=1) — 'Things unlock basically every step of the way until endgame'

learn.practice: Offer build presets and a training dummy so players can test a rule set safely before a run.
learn.evidence: https://steamcommunity.com/app/2494810/reviews (recommendation 234243250; via store.steampowered.com/appreviews/2494810?json=1) — 'free respecs, build presets, solid lootfilter, training dummy'
